"'''Save Your Tears'''" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [[the Weeknd]] from his fourth studio album, ''[[After Hours (The Weeknd album)|After Hours]]'' (2020). It was released to Dutch contemporary hit radio on August 9, 2020, as the album's fifth and final single. The song was written and produced by the Weeknd, [[Max Martin]], and [[Oscar Holter]], with [[Belly (rapper)|Belly]] and [[DaHeala]] receiving additional writing credits.

In the United States, the solo version peaked at number four on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. A remix with American singer [[Ariana Grande]] was released on April 23, 2021, and propelled the song to number one on the Hot 100, marking both artists' sixth number-one single on the chart. This also made ''After Hours'' the first album since [[Drake (musician)|Drake]]'s ''[[Scorpion (Drake album)|Scorpion]]'' in 2018 to have three singles from the same album to reach number one. The song has since been certified triple platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]].

"Save Your Tears" was the [[List of best-selling singles#Best-selling singles by year worldwide|best-selling global single]] of 2021, earning 2.15 billion subscription streams equivalents globally according to the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] (IFPI). "Save Your Tears" and its remix with Grande peaked at number one in 18 countries and reached the top ten in 33 others. In the Weeknd's native country Canada, the remix peaked at number one on the [[Canadian Hot 100]], where it became both the Weeknd and Grande's sixth chart-topper. The remix also peaked at number one on the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]], becoming the Weeknd's first number-one single on the chart and Grande's second.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' hailed the song as the best track on ''After Hours'', stating: "Although 'Save Your Tears' is one of the most [[Pop music|pop]]-driven songs on the album, the Weeknd doesn't hold back when it comes to the rather cold nature he usually finds himself adopting when it comes to his lovers. The production remains upbeat and steady the entire time, thanks to work from [[Max Martin]], [[Oscar Holter]], [[DaHeala]], and The Weeknd himself, combining the best of his old content and some newer, more mainstream-driven sounds".<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/the-weeknd-after-hours-every-song-ranked-9339446|title= Every Song Ranked on The Weeknd's 'After Hours': Critic's Picks|website= Billboard Magazine|date= March 20, 2020|access-date= June 3, 2020|archive-date= January 12, 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210112073747/https://www.billboard.com/amp/articles/columns/hip-hop/9339446/the-weeknd-after-hours-every-song-ranked|url-status= live}}</ref> Craig Jenkins of ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]'' raved, "The Weeknd perfects the [[kitsch]]y [[1980s in music|'80s]] genre experiment with 'Save Your Tears', a gutting breakup tune gorgeous and simple enough to stand alongside peak '80s pop like [[the Cars]]' '[[You Might Think]]' (and slick enough to swipe a bit of melody from [[Wham!]]'s '[[Everything She Wants]]' in the chorus). The piece concocts sound informed by both [[Trap music|trap]] and [[dance music]], encased in dense atmospherics, and heavy on crisp, bright keys".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2020/04/the-weeknd-after-hours-pnd-partymobile-album-review.html|title=The Weeknd and PND's Dirtbag R&B Is Hard to Beat|website=Vulture Magazine|date=April 3, 2020|access-date=June 3, 2020|archive-date=June 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200603110234/https://www.vulture.com/amp/2020/04/the-weeknd-after-hours-pnd-partymobile-album-review.html|url-status=live}}</ref> "'Save Your Tears' has both tonal echoes of [[Depeche Mode]]'s melancholy and a nod to 'Everything She Wants' by Wham!, exhibiting shimmery mid-80s luxuriance", praised ''[[The New York Times]]'' editor [[Jon Caramanica]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/01/arts/music/the-weeknd-after-hours-review.amp.html|title=The Weeknd's Gleamy, Seamy Pop Returns|website=New York Times|date=April 2020|access-date=June 3, 2020|last1=Caramanica|first1=Jon|archive-date=December 13, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213094113/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/01/arts/music/the-weeknd-after-hours-review.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Slant Magazine|Slant]]'' columnist Seth Wilson observed, "'Save Your Tears' revels in spite, flaunting how over-it Tesfaye is in front of his ex while teasing the possibility of reconciliation. Tesfaye's distinct brand of [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] consistently draws from other genres, but hearing him embrace a straight-up [[synth-rock]] sound here is an exciting change of pace".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/music/review-the-weeknd-after-hours-is-a-triumphant-depiction-of-heartbreak/amp/|title=Review: The Weeknd's After Hours Is a Triumphant Depiction of Heartbreak|website=Slant Magazine|date=March 28, 2020 |access-date=June 3, 2020|archive-date=April 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418103746/https://www.slantmagazine.com/music/review-the-weeknd-after-hours-is-a-triumphant-depiction-of-heartbreak/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref> "He draws on [[synth-pop]] nostalgia to mirror the tragic glitz of '80s [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]: the plinking synths and slick [[Clapping|hand-claps]] of 'Save Your Tears' evokes a long-lost Wham! track. His bleeding-heart melodies and unforgettable hooks remind us why we keep listening to the '80s first place", exclaimed ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' writer Isabella Herrera.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/the-weeknd-after-hours/amp|title=The Weeknd After Hours|website=Pitchfork|access-date=June 3, 2020|archive-date=June 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611063554/https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/the-weeknd-after-hours/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref> Jem Aswad of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' commented, "'Save Your Tears', which could have been an [[MTV]] staple in the early '80s, is begging for period-appropriate videos. The record has thwacking [[electronic percussion]] and the [[vocoder]] hearkening back to [[Electric Light Orchestra]]'s '[[Mr. Blue Sky]]'".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2020/music/reviews/the-weeknd-after-hours-album-review-1203539981/|title=The Weeknd's 'After Hours': Album Review|website=Variety|date=March 20, 2020|access-date=June 3, 2020|archive-date=June 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200601233806/https://variety.com/2020/music/reviews/the-weeknd-after-hours-album-review-1203539981/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Mark Richardson from ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' asserted that "'Save Your Tears' includes soaring melodies that provide ample opportunity for Mr. Tesfaye to show off his vocal range, being used on television singing competitions. By design, it is big and broad, less specific lyrically and further from the shadowy persona at the heart of the Weeknd—Mr. Tesfaye often seems downright affable here. sections.wikitext:
The official music video for "Save Your Tears" was first teased by the Weeknd as being on its way through his social media platforms on January 4, 2021.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=TheWeeknd|number=1346247109175984128|title=SAVE YOUR TEARS. TOMORROW.|date=January 4, 2021|accessdate=January 6, 2021}}</ref> It was released the following day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/watch-the-weeknd-new-save-your-tears-video/|title=Watch the Weeknd's New "Save Your Tears" Video|first=Matthew|last=Strauss|website=Pitchfork|date=January 5, 2021|access-date=January 6, 2021|archive-date=January 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210105192643/https://pitchfork.com/news/watch-the-weeknd-new-save-your-tears-video/|url-status=live}}</ref> Prosthetic Renaissance Makeup-FX Studio designer [[Mike Marino (make-up artist)|Mike Marino]] crafted the signature look resembling plastic surgery. The process commenced as he shaped a general sculpture of the Weeknd's modified visage, then created the prosthetics. Four primary prosthetic components were involved: one for each lip; one for the nose, eyebrows, and forehead; and one for the cheeks and chin. After they were applied to the Weeknd's face, makeup was utilized to make them blend in.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/music/the-weeknd-save-your-tears-look-created-special-effects-prosthetics/|title=Here's How The Weeknd's Extreme 'Save Your Tears' Plastic-Surgery Look Was Created|first=Derrick|last=Rossignol|website=Uproxx|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=February 26, 2021|archive-date=January 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106193642/https://uproxx.com/music/the-weeknd-save-your-tears-look-created-special-effects-prosthetics/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Directed by Cliqua, the video sees the Weeknd wearing a diamond-adorned version of his original red-jacketed outfit. The bruises on his face are no longer present, although his character has apparently undergone a bizarre plastic surgery. He performs in a lavish nightclub occupied by formally attired members wearing glittery, full-face masks that pay homage to scenes from [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s final film, ''[[Eyes Wide Shut]]''; his backing band is also wearing masks. He wanders out into the motionless, seated crowd, guzzling one person's champagne and laying his arm on the head of another until he notices a gorgeously brilliant, maskless woman in the audience (played by Bianca Rojas) and guides her onstage. While they initially are dancing joyfully, the camera soon reveals that the Weeknd is hiding a pistol behind his back. The lights go out and when the lights are turned back on, the Weeknd has placed his gun in one of her hands with him pointing the gun at his own head. The woman realizes this and shrieks. The scene concludes with the Weeknd holding the pistol to his own head. As the song finishes, he pulls the trigger, releasing confetti. The assembly applauds apprehensively at first, then enthusiastically.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/the-weeknd-save-your-tears-music-video-1109860/|title=Save Your Tears Music Video|first=John|last=Blistein|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=January 5, 2021|accessdate=April 22, 2021|archive-date=May 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503201503/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/the-weeknd-save-your-tears-music-video-1109860/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The second remix of "Save Your Tears", a collaboration with American singer-songwriter [[Ariana Grande]], was released on April 23, 2021, with an accompanying animated music video depicting Grande as a [[gynoid]] in the process of [[Industrial robot|automated assembly]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/sthe-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-song-video-1160220/|title=See the Weeknd, Ariana Grande's Animated 'Save Your Tears' Remix Video|first=Althea|last=Legaspi|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=April 23, 2021|access-date=April 27, 2021|archive-date=April 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429171228/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/sthe-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-song-video-1160220/|url-status=live}}</ref> It was included on the deluxe version of the Weeknd's fourth studio album ''[[After Hours (The Weeknd album)|After Hours]]''. The song marks the third collaboration between the Weeknd and Grande, after "[[Love Me Harder]]" (2014) and "[[Off the Table]]" (2020).<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Mamo|first=Heran|date=April 23, 2021|title=The Weeknd Drops 'Save Your Tears' Remix With Ariana Grande: Stream It Now|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-stream-9561503/|magazine=Billboard|access-date=April 23, 2021|archive-date=April 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423040929/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/pop/9561503/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-stream/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The remix was a commercial success in the United States, peaking at number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for two weeks. It became the sixth number-one single on the chart for both artists, and made ''After Hours'' the first album since [[Drake (musician)|Drake]]'s ''[[Scorpion (Drake album)|Scorpion]]'' in 2018 to have three singles from the same album to reach number one. The remix ranked as the second best-performing song of the year on the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2021|year-end Hot 100 chart of 2021]]. In the Weeknd's native country Canada, it peaked at number one on the ''Billboard'' [[Canadian Hot 100]], where it became both the Weeknd and Grande's sixth chart-topper. The remix also topped the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]], marking the Weeknd's first number-one single on the chart and Grande's second.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' staff member Katie Atkinson complimented, "Ariana Grande brings her ethereal vocals to the song".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/media/podcasts/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-musical-history-pop-shop-podcast-9563427|title=The Weeknd & Ariana Grande Bring Years of Musical History to 'Save Your Tears' Remix|first=Katie|last=Atkinson|magazine=Billboard|date=April 27, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=September 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928095727/https://www.billboard.com/amp/articles/columns/podcasts/9563427/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-musical-history-pop-shop-podcast|url-status=live}}</ref> "The Weeknd and Ariana Grande's third collaboration will have you smiling all year long", ''Billboard'' journalist Gab Ginsberg exclaimed.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/save-your-tears-remix-best-music-moments-april-23-9561825|title=The 13 Best Things That Happened in Music This Week (April 23)|first=Gab|last=Ginsburg|magazine=Billboard|date=April 23, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=May 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508081343/https://www.billboard.com/amp/articles/news/9561825/save-your-tears-remix-best-music-moments-april-23|url-status=live}}</ref> Natalia Barr of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' hailed it as one of the best new pop records, "the two singers have reunited on an updated piece from the Weeknd's [[New wave music|new wave]]-inspired album from last year, ''[[After Hours (The Weeknd album)|After Hours]]''. Grande adds her sultry vocals to the song's second verse and chorus".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/doja-cat-prince-best-songs-spotify-11619785572|title=From Doja Cat to Prince: the Best Songs You Should Be Listening to Right Now|first=Natalia|last=Barr|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=April 30, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307143511/https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/doja-cat-prince-best-songs-spotify-11619785572|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[NME]]'' columnist Will Lavin noted, "Grande adds a fresh and husky verse of her own to the remix".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/the-weeknd-teases-save-your-tears-remix-featuring-ariana-grande-2923716|title=Ariana Grande adds a fresh verse to The Weeknd's 'Save Your Tears' on new remix|first=Will|last=Lavin|website=NME|date=April 23, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307143511/https://www.nme.com/news/music/the-weeknd-teases-save-your-tears-remix-featuring-ariana-grande-2923716|url-status=live}}</ref>

Monica Sisavat from ''[[PopSugar]]'' described the remix as pure perfection, "Let's just say their voices together are just chef's kiss."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.popsugar.com/entertainment/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-48277641/amp|title=The Weeknd and Ariana Grande's Latest Collab Is Finally Here, and It's a Bop|first=Monica|last=Sisavat|website=PopSugar|date=April 23, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307143514/https://www.popsugar.com/entertainment/the-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-48277641/amp|url-status=live}}</ref> "The pair's vocals intermingle on the wistful, synth-laden track as they harmonize," ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' editor Althea Legaspi stated.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/sthe-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-song-video-1160220/|title=See the Weeknd, Ariana Grande's Animated 'Save Your Tears' Remix Video|first=Althea|last=Legaspi|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=April 23, 2021|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307143511/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/sthe-weeknd-ariana-grande-save-your-tears-remix-song-video-1160220/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Apple Music]] celebrated the composition, "'Save Your Tears' is just as dreamy and lush as the 2020 original, but Grande's vocal acrobatics lend it a new dynamic—it's a duet now, two former lovers looking up at the same night sky, talking back and forth at a distance".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/playlist/a-list-pop/pl.5ee8333dbe944d9f9151e97d92d1ead9|title=A-List-Pop|website=Apple Music|accessdate=May 3, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307152017/https://music.apple.com/us/playlist/a-list-pop/pl.5ee8333dbe944d9f9151e97d92d1ead9|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the release of the remix with [[Ariana Grande]], "Save Your Tears" reached the top of the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 on the issue dated May 8, 2021. Additionally, it also topped the ''Billboard'' [[Digital Songs|Digital Song Sales]] chart, becoming Grande's eighth and the Weeknd's sixth chart-topping single. With eight number-one singles each, Grande joined [[Lady Gaga]] as a female artist with the fifth-most number-one singles on the ''Billboard'' Digital Song Sales Chart.<ref>{{cite web|last=McIntyre|first=Hugh|date=May 10, 2021|title=Ariana Grande Ties Lady Gaga For The Fifth-Most No. 1s On The Sales Chart Among Women|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2021/05/10/ariana-grande-ties-lady-gaga-for-the-fifth-most-no-1s-on-the-sales-chart-among-women/|access-date=May 12, 2021|website=Forbes|archive-date=May 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511065934/https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2021/05/10/ariana-grande-ties-lady-gaga-for-the-fifth-most-no-1s-on-the-sales-chart-among-women/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the release of the remix with Ariana Grande, "Save Your Tears" reached the top of the Billboard Hot 100 on the issue dated May 8, 2021. It became the sixth number-one hit of both the Weeknd and Grande (the latter of whom was credited on the track on the chart for the first time, as the remix drew the majority of the title's overall activity in the tracking week). Additionally, it also topped the Billboard Digital Song Sales chart, becoming Grande's eighth and the Weeknd's sixth chart-topping single. With eight number-one singles each, Grande joined Lady Gaga as a female artist with the fifth-most number-one singles on the Billboard Digital Song Sales Chart.

The Weeknd also became the first artist since Drake to earn three number-one singles from one album following his recent singles from After Hours, "Heartless" and "Blinding Lights" reaching number one. He also became the first artist to have three number ones from one album in three different years since Janet Jackson's album Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation 1814. Joining Paul McCartney, Grande became just the second act and the first woman to earn three number-one duets in Billboard Hot 100 history. This was also Grande's third number-one duet within a year's span making her the artist with the fastest accumulation of three chart-topping duets. It remained at number one for a second consecutive week, drawing 22.4 million streams, 68.5 million radio airplay and 9,600 downloads on the week ending May 9, 2021. On the Rolling Stone Top 100 Songs chart, the song peaked at number 2 following the release of the Ariana Grande remix.

Following the release of the remix with Grande, the song also peaked at the top spot of the Billboard Global 200, becoming the Weeknd's first and Grande's second number-one single. It also became the first male-female duet to reach the number one position. Joining BTS, Grande became just the second act and the first woman to earn multiple number-one hits on the Billboard Global 200 Chart. Joining Drake, Justin Bieber and BTS, Grande also became just the fourth act and the first woman to earn at least four top ten hits on Billboard Global 200 survey. Additionally, it reached a new peak of number two on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart. "Save Your Tears" has spent 27 weeks in the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100.

In the singer's native country of Canada, "Save Your Tears" rose to number one following the release of the Ariana Grande remix on the issue dated May 8, 2021, becoming the sixth number one hit of both the Weeknd and Grande. It became the second chart-topper from the parent album After Hours, after its biggest hit single "Blinding Lights". Additionally, it also topped the Canadian Digital Songs Sales chart.
